package_info.package_versions: unknown (all published versions as of incident)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were published to the npm repository with the intent to deliver the TurkoRat info-stealer malware. They are designed to trick developers into installing them via social engineering (typosquatting, high version numbers), and contain code that exfiltrates sensitive information from infected systems.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code reads browser cookies from the local filesystem and sends them via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, enabling credential and session exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing browser cookies and exfiltrating them to an external server is a classic info-stealer behavior and is not expected in legitimate npm packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access sensitive browser data or transmit it to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate browser automation or backup tools may access cookies, but never exfiltrate them to untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Sends data to hardcoded external domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code reads credential and cryptocurrency wallet files from the user's home directory and exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST to a malicious server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials and wallet files is a hallmark of info-stealer malware and is never appropriate in a general-purpose npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or transmit user credentials or wallet data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may access such files, but only with explicit user consent and never send them to untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Reads sensitive credential and wallet files
Exfiltrates data to hardcoded remote server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for environment variables indicative of sandbox or CI environments and terminates execution to evade automated analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks are common in malware to avoid detection and are rarely justified in open-source packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not attempt to detect or evade sandboxes or CI environments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some performance-sensitive packages may avoid running in CI, but this is rare and should be documented.
key_indicators: Checks for SANDBOX or CI environment variables
Obfuscates true behavior from automated analysis

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package (nodejs-encrypt-agent or nodejs-cookie-proxy-agent).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on the developer's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code reads sensitive data (browser cookies, credentials, wallet files) from the filesystem.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code exfiltrates harvested data to a hardcoded external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials, cookies, and wallet data.

attack_chain.action: Malware checks for sandbox or CI environments and terminates if detected to avoid analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reduces likelihood of detection by automated security tools.

behavioral_signatures: npm package accessing browser cookies or credential files at import-time or runtime
Exfiltration of local files to hardcoded external domains via HTTPS POST
Anti-sandbox or anti-analysis environment checks and early process termination
file_indicators: Presence of anti-analysis code checking for SANDBOX or CI environment variables
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains immediately after package import or install
Connections to domains associated with known info-stealer C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for code that accesses sensitive browser, credential, or wallet files and sends their contents to external servers. Flag packages that contain anti-sandbox or anti-analysis logic. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected outbound HTTPS POST requests to untrusted domains during or immediately after package installation or import. Employ static and dynamic analysis to identify file access and exfiltration patterns in package code.
